clues: Home to MacGillycuddy’s Reeks, the highest mountain range in Ireland.
Carrauntoohil, Ireland’s highest mountain, is here.
fact: Carrauntoohil stands 1,038.6 metres tall, the central peak of MacGillycuddy’s Reeks on the Iveragh Peninsula.

clues: Fewer people live here than in any other county on the island: 35,199 in 2022.
fact: Leitrim had 35,199 people in Census 2022. Next smallest: Longford (46,751) and Carlow (61,968).

clues: About 40,000 interlocking basalt columns stand on its north coast.
The Giant’s Causeway, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1986, is here.
fact: The Giant’s Causeway’s roughly 40,000 basalt columns were declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1986.

clues: Its hurlers have won a record 36 All-Ireland senior titles.
fact: Kilkenny’s 36 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championships are a national record, making it the most successful county in the history of hurling.

clues: At 7,508 km², it’s the largest county in Ireland.
fact: Cork covers 7,508 km², well ahead of Galway (6,151 km²) and Mayo (5,588 km²).

clues: A 5,000-year-old tomb here lights up for about 17 minutes at the winter solstice.
Newgrange is here.
fact: Newgrange was built around 3100 BC. At the winter solstice the rising sun shines through its roofbox and floods the inner chamber for about 17 minutes.

clues: The smallest county in Ireland, at just 826 km².
fact: Louth covers just 826 km². Carlow (897 km²) and Dublin (922 km²) are the next smallest.

clues: Its caves anchor the world’s first international, cross-border geopark.
The Marble Arch Caves are here, near Florencecourt.
fact: The Marble Arch Caves Global Geopark joined UNESCO’s geopark network in 2004. In 2008 it stretched across the border into Cavan, becoming the first international geopark in the world.

clues: It has the highest share of unpaid carers in the Republic: 7% of its people.
fact: In Census 2022, 7% of people in Mayo were unpaid carers, the highest rate in the country. Dublin City was lowest, at 5%.

clues: Its sea cliffs run for about 14 km and reach 214 metres high.
The Cliffs of Moher are here, on the edge of the Burren.
fact: The Cliffs of Moher run for about 14 km and peak at 214 metres, just north of O’Brien’s Tower. They get around 1.5 million visits a year.

clues: The River Shannon traditionally rises here.
The Shannon Pot is here.
fact: The Shannon Pot, a small pool in the hills, is the traditional source of the River Shannon.

clues: Brian Boru was crowned King of Munster here in 977.
The Rock of Cashel is here.
fact: The Rock of Cashel was the seat of the kings of Munster. Legend says it landed there when St Patrick banished Satan from a cave in the Devil’s Bit mountain.

clues: The most northerly point of mainland Ireland is here.
Malin Head is here, on the Inishowen peninsula.
fact: Malin Head is the most northerly point of mainland Ireland. The tiny island of Inishtrahull lies further north still.

clues: St Ciarán founded a monastery on the Shannon here in 544.
Clonmacnoise is here, south of Athlone.
fact: St Ciarán founded Clonmacnoise in 544, on the River Shannon south of Athlone.

clues: It had the lowest share of homes with broadband in Census 2022: 72%.
fact: Broadband ranged from 91% of homes in Dún Laoghaire-Rathdown to 72% here. Nationally it was almost 80%.
